newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Rolls-Royce engine glitch prompts HK checks.
newsitem.headline: Rolls-Royce engine glitch prompts HK checks.

text.p: Hong Kong Aircraft Engineering Co Ltd (Haeco) said on Wednesday it was working with Rolls-Royce Plc on problems affecting the British firm's Trent 700 engines after a series of single-engine landings.
"We're working with Rolls at the moment on gearbox problems," a Haeco spokesman told Reuters. He would not elaborate.
Haeco maintains aircraft at Hong Kong's Kai Tak airport.
Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd has experienced problems with gearbox bearings on Airbus A330-300 aircraft using Trent 700 engines, Cathay spokesman Kwan Chuk-fai told Reuters.
Cathay operates 11 A330-300s using Trent 700 engines, while its sister airline Hong Kong Dragon Airlines (Dragonair) uses four.
Trent 800 and other Rolls-Royce engines were not affected by the problem, Cathay said in a statement.
A spokesman for Rolls-Royce said the gearbox bearings on the Trent 700 engines were being replaced and the problem was being investigated.

Kwan said the airline had shutdowns involving Trent 700 engines, including a single-engine landing at Bangkok last week and another two weeks ago when a flight to the Philippines had to turn back to Hong Kong.
A Vietnam-bound airliner had to make a single-engine landing last November, he added.
In April, a Dragonair airliner suffered a similar gearbox problem while flying from Hong Kong to Shanghai, the South China Morning Post newspaper said on Wednesday.

"I would stress that engine shutdown does not pose a danger to passengers because all modern aircraft -- particularly those twin-engine aircraft -- are designed to be able to fly and land on their remaining engine," Kwan told Reuters.

All Cathay flights using Airbus A330s with Trent engines were now flying no more than one hour from the nearest airport, Kwan said. The only route to be affected would be Hong Kong-Colombo, which might take longer than usual, he said.
Haeco is 25 percent owned by Cathay Pacific and 27 percent by Swire Pacific Ltd. Last year, it formed a 50/50 joint venture with a Rolls-Royce subsidiary.
Cathay Pacific's shares were unchanged at HK$11.85 at midday on Wednesday.
